newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: United urges National not to delay NZ tax cuts.
newsitem.headline: United urges National not to delay NZ tax cuts.

text.p: United New Zealand leader Peter Dunne said on Monday he had urged Prime Minister Jim Bolger not to delay or ditch the next round of tax cuts in order to ingratiate the National Party with New Zealand First leader Winston Peters.

"The National Party campaigned hard on those cuts, and they were right to do so....To now suggest that the tax cuts may be put at risk so that a deal can be cemented with New Zealand First is simply not on."

The Dominion newspaper's lead story on Monday reported the National Party was considering delaying or ultimately scrapping its second round of tax cuts to accommodate NZ First's demands for increased spending and compulsory superannuation.
Dunne said the tax cuts, the first round of which was implemented on July 1, provided much-needed relief for low and middle income New Zealanders.

He said if National wanted to proceed with a compulsory superannuation scheme it should establish a working party to develop the scheme. Labour Party leader Helen Clark has also suggested a working party on the issue.
Dunne said compulsory superannuation could then be introduced from July 1, 1998, as an alternative to further tax cuts after next year's round.
He urged National to stick to its principles and deliver the lower taxes it had promised.
"Any lessening of that position by National will be an expedient cop out, and will be seen for what it is," Dunne said.
NZ First is negotiating with both National and Labour in the bid to form a new government after October's inconclusive general election.
